en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.33.
Parāmāsa-duka, etc.
Dependent on a state that is not adhered to (*aparāmāsa*), a state that is not adhered to arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five;
... [and so on] ... under resultant condition there is one; ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance condition there are five.
Dependent on a state that is not adhered to, a state that is not adhered to arises by way of root condition.

A state arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that is neither misapprehension nor misapprehended, there arises a state that is neither misapprehension nor misapprehended by way of the root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither misapprehension nor misapprehended, there arises a state that is neither misapprehension nor misapprehended, and a state that is neither misapprehended nor misapprehension.
And states arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to nor-attachment, there arises a state that is neither-clung-to nor-attachment by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-attachment nor-clung-to and a state that is neither-clung-to nor-attachment, there arises a state that is neither-clung-to nor-attachment by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of cause, five; ... pe ... in the case of result, one; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, five.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, there arises a state dissociated from the taints and not adhered to by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, [there arises] a state dissociated from the taints...
A state that is not adhered to arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints and not adhered to,
there arise states that are dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, as well as states that are dissociated from the taints but adhered to,
by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*parāmāsa*) and not adhered to (*na-āparāmaṭṭha*), there arises a state dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on states both dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, and dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, there arises a state dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, by way of root condition.
[Under] root [condition] there are five; under object condition, two ... [etc. ... under non-disappearance condition, five.
The Section on Misapprehension is finished.
